response.query: How will we adjust for cluster designs or repeated measures (explicit design-effect formula, assumed ICC values, and rules for effective sample size)?
response.answer: To adjust for cluster designs or repeated measures, use design-effect formula, assumed intraclass correlation values, and calculate effective sample size accordingly. Design effect accounts for clustering, while intraclass correlation measures similarity within clusters.

Further study is required to be deeply understand the experience of colorectal survivors’ adaptation and transition to their life after cancer treatment and develop arbitration plan for im-proving the colorectal cancer survivors’ quality of life P302 COUPLES’ EXPERIENCE OF UNCERTAINTY IN FACING GYNECOLOGICAL CANCER Yingzi Zhang, PhD, RN, University of Rochester, Roch-ester, NY; Sally Norton, PhD, RN, FNAP, FPCN, FAAN, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY; Marie Flannery, PhD, RN, AOCN®, University of Rochester School of Nursing, Rochester, NY; Rachel Carter, MS, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY; Charles Kamen, PhD, MPH, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY Research Uncertainty is common and distressing for patients and their partners, which causes clinically significant levels of depression and anxiety.
